In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) how to extract meaningful information from a dataset characterized by only a few features, (2) how to identify and describe the most significant user habits, (3) how to provide a simple and effective graphical representation of clusters and knowledge discovery results, which can be understood and employed by the analyst.

the paper presents a new framework for identifying patterns and habits in mobile phone users, which is capable of automatically discovering the most suitable dissimilarity measure for each cluster.
, in this work we have proposed a novel framework for data mining of CDR data, which can be used for understanding the habits of a mobile user.
the proposed approach is able to identify the most significant patterns in the data and to extract the user's habits, without requiring any additional information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to extract useful information from CDR data, without the need to know a priori any specific application context.
we are able to extract meaningful information from the CDRs and to provide a tool that can be used for practical applications.
we have shown how to extract useful knowledge from the CDRs of a single user, by using unsupervised learning techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed framework is capable to extract useful information from the data, even in the case of a very limited number of features, without any a priori assumptions on the applicative domain.
it can be applied to a wide set of problems in the telecommunications field, and in general in the field of big data analysis.
the data mining procedure can be successfully applied to a real-world dataset, with the aim of discovering users' habits and of building their characterizing profiles.
